title: SceneClaw: from a driving video to a 4D code world
subtitle: Waymo Open Dataset, San Francisco, daytime · 199 frames at 10 fps · single agent session (v23.6)
task: Reconstruct this driving clip as an editable 4D blocks world.

steps.label: Plan
steps.text:
The clip is reconstructed in four phases, each concluded by an explicit acceptance check: (A) camera, ground and road; (B) buildings and street furniture; (C) vehicles, pedestrians and vegetation; (D) a whole-scene review, followed by export to `scene_world.py`. Perception tools only propose; each proposal is verified against overlays on the camera frames and against the bird's-eye view (BEV) before it is accepted.
Initial inspection: an 8-frame overview, ego speed and yaw, camera pose discontinuities, and a metric-scale test.
kv: height 2.27 m, pitch 0.94 deg downward, rmse 0.018

steps.label: Ground surface and lane-marking evidence
steps.code:
# SAW: a boulevard with a tram median on the left; the ego
#      vehicle is stationary behind a Kia until ~f80, then
#      proceeds straight through a junction (~f110-140)

# 1. fit one ground surface to DA3 road depth and ego path
g = ground.fit(c4)
ground.install(c4, g)

# 2. define a road frame: s along the drive, t to the left
F = roadmodel.frame(c4, curved=False)

# 3. lift the Vistas lane-marking pixels onto the ground
P = roadtools.paint_points(c4)

# 4. render them in (s, t) from above to read lane offsets
png = roadtools.evidence_bev(c4, P, F)

steps.label: Road model from measured offsets
steps.code:
# SAW: marking peaks (t_peaks) at t = +1.7 / -2.2 / -6.0 m,
#      yellow at +2.1, median curb at +3.3 / +2.5, right
#      kerb at -12.7

# 1. encode the cross-section as a spec, one line per offset
L = []
L.append(dict(t=1.9, type="road_line",
              subtype="double_yellow", ...))
L.append(dict(t=3.3, type="road_edge", ...))
for tt in (-2.1, -6.0, -9.3):
    L.append(dict(t=tt, type="road_line",
                  subtype="dashed_white", ...))
L.append(dict(t=-12.7, type="road_edge", ...))

# 2. build the lines along the frame, with junction mouths
spec = dict(lines=L, mouths=[...], s_range=(-60, 200))
roadmodel.build(c4, F, spec)

# 3. project the lines into four frames for verification
roadmodel.check(c4, frames=[0, 100, 150, 198])

steps.label: Projected lines against the markings
steps.text: Frames 0, 100 and 150: the projected lines coincide with the markings. Frame 198: the lines deviate approximately 1 m to the left of the dashes, and the median kerb is absent near the camera.
kv: 52 road lines and edges (30 observed segments, 22 extrapolated beyond the view)

steps.label: Road curvature from lane-marking offsets
steps.code:
# SAW: frames 0 / 100 / 150 agree with the markings; in
#      frame 198 the lines deviate ~1 m to the left

# 1. replace the straight frame by one following the ego path
F = roadmodel.frame(c4, curved=True)
roadmodel.build(c4, F, spec)
#    -> frame 180: lines still diverge from the markings far ahead

# 2. measure the lateral offset of the markings over s 90-200
pr = roadtools.offset_profile(F, P["white"][:, :2],
                              90, 200, ...)
#    -> t constant up to s 125, then +0.3 to +1.5 m to the left

# 3. re-align the frame: 6 deg left curve from s 145, R 200 m
F0 = F
F = geomtools.frame_bend(F0, 145, 200, 6.0)
roadmodel.build(c4, F, spec)

# 4. re-render frame 180 for comparison with the image
c4.still(180)

steps.label: Vehicle tracks verified with D-FINE
steps.code:
# SAW: phase B complete: 16 traffic lights, 15 signs,
#      buildings, walls, gate wall and median railing

# 1. vehicle tracks from the tools: WildDet3D 3D boxes,
#    associated over time by SAM3-video identities
trs = [t for t in kit4d.tracks_from_tools(vid)
       if t.type != "TYPE_PEDESTRIAN"]
c4.tracks = [...] + trs

# 2. test each world box against an independent 2D
#    detector (D-FINE)
rows = vehtools.dfine_check(c4)

# 3. crop sheet of the weakly supported tracks
vehtools.dfine_sheet(c4, rows)
